Triangulated from two or more solved photos; sight lines cross within about 1-3 m, so the position is good to roughly +/-10 m once picking error is allowed for. Why Roberts Hall: two full stories about 80 ft long as scaled from the photo (the footprint uses the Cow Boy's 24 x 75) with few upper windows (a hall, not hotel rooms), a raised front on its south end, long axis north-south; still standing about 1905 (Roberts Hall stood until 1923, while the hotel burned in 1897); next to today's Old Town Hall Theater (Roberts Hall may be the "town hall" of a 1903 stereo, still to be checked); near the hotel and in view of the railroad (HMdb). Further support (Oct 16): Hagedorn's 1919 photo of "Bill Williams' saloon" (Houghton 3013539) shows a two-story frame hall with a fanlight in its front gable and a door to the upper floor; in his 1919 overview (Houghton 3013472) a dark two-story gabled building of that form, long axis north-south, stands south of the Rough Riders and north of the depot, which is where D2 is. The Roberts Hall marker (HMdb 88016) stands in a small park next to the Old Town Hall Theater, about 10 m from this point. Location raised to B; the Cow Boy's "lot 7, block 17" remains unexplained. Lot check (Oct 16): the triangulated position falls on today's lot 7 (parcel "7-8") of Block 13 - the same lot number the Cow Boy gives (Cow Boy 1884-06-26: "It is located on lot 7, block 17, and creates a very favorable impression from the railroad, standing as it does in full view."). Today's Block 17, in the southeast of town, is open sagebrush in the 1885 overview (SHSND 00042-00195), so the hall cannot have stood there. Either the 1883 plat numbered this block 17, or the paper misprinted 13 as 17. Neither block 13 nor block 17 is on the 1883 "Price of Lots" list (TRMF-01), so both were held back from public sale. The Historic Medora "Billings County Courthouse" panel shows a winter photo captioned "Roberts Hall housed the first county offices" (the panel dates the county seat to 1886 in a separate sentence): a two-story front-gabled frame hall with an upper-floor door, the same form as Hagedorn's 1919 "Bill Williams' saloon". features.name: Cooling house (1883)
features.built_text: built from June 1883; finished when SHSND 00042-00188 was taken (1883)
features.use: refrigerated cooling house for dressed beef, with a car-loading platform
features.evidence: Located by its cupola, triangulated in the solved overviews SHSND 00042-00071 and -00195 and the two fitted plant photos (00042-00074, MHS 72460); good to about +/-2 m. Its south wall abuts the north-east corner of the main packing house.
features.notes: Added from the 2026 photo audit. A refrigerator car (NP 4800) stands at its loading platform in 00042-00150.

massing.src: estimated from the period photographs (see Appearance)

style.basis: SHSND 00042-00150 and -00188 (1883), seen behind the plant in 00042-00074/-00075 and MHS 72460: a near-cubic block of painted clapboard, eave about 9 m (scaled from the refrigerator car beside it), a hipped roof with a square louvred cupola, a loading platform on trestle legs at car-floor height. The walls are nearly blank in 00188, 00150 and 00075 (one or two openings a face, not a window grid). Cupola: small in 1883 (00188: about 1.8 m wide, 1.6 m body, 1.5 m cap), much larger in 1885-87 (00074 against the chimney, 00075 against the building: about 3.2 m square, 2.3 m louvred body, 2.1 m steep cap with a finial), so enlarged or rebuilt between 1883 and 1885; the model dates the two sizes at 1885.0

features.name: Plant tower (east)
features.use: unknown (a walkway from the main house reached it)
features.evidence: A tall narrow dark tower with a pyramid cap stands at the west end of the east building, reached by an open walkway about 8-9 m up (SHSND 00042-00074, MHS 72460, 00042-00180). Its peak (about 11.4 m) is located by joint solve of the plant photos and the overviews (+/-3 m). A lower, front-gabled board base (about 3.6 m wide, eave about 5.3 m, gable to the south with a ladder on it in MHS 72460) stands at its foot.
